Forecast Discussion

A dry front crossed from the northwest overnight. The wind behind it is the story today, and it eases this evening as high pressure builds into the Ohio Valley.

High pressure sits over the Southern Appalachians Tuesday and moves to the coast Wednesday. Afternoons warm nicely. Valleys turn frosty at night.

A cold front crosses the mountains around midday Thursday. Showers develop late Wednesday night and Thursday morning, especially on the west side of the Appalachians, with a lull for the east side of the mountains Thursday afternoon. Low pressure forms along the front and deepens off the Mid-Atlantic coast Thursday night as much colder air pours in. Rain showers change to snow showers from west to east around midnight.

Snow showers continue Friday and Friday night on a cold, windy northwest flow. Snow showers Saturday taper to flurries Saturday evening. Accumulations focus on the Tennessee line and the Grayson Highlands, with little or none east of the Blue Ridge.

We are balancing several factors in this event's forecast: 1) Relatively warm Great Lakes water will enhance moisture in the air that reaches us Friday and Saturday. 2) Elevations below 3800' during the daytime Friday will be in a "snow and melt" scenario until the cover of darkness. 3) The moist flow off the Great Lakes is limited in time--about 36 hours. and 4) The ground is warm. Putting all that together, here's a concept map for what we expect. Don't take it too literally with 4 days to go before the event.

Sunday starts cold and sunny, and afternoons recover quickly as high pressure settles overhead. The Snowman-O-Mometer is out of hibernation--our 5-day snow outlook.
